newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government to buy more rubber to aid prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai government to buy more rubber to aid prices.

text.p: The Thai government has bought 26,400 tonnes of rubber since March 5 to shore up domestic rubber prices and intends to buy more in the future, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Wednesday.
The latest purchase was made on Tuesday when the government concluded a deal to buy 7,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber at 123.5 US cents a kg.
The purchases so far were separate from another scheme under which the government guaranteed a minimum price for local rubber at 27 baht a kg versus 25 baht previously.
"If we combined the purchases under the two programmes together, it would top 30,000 tonnes," the ministry official told Reuters.
"We intend to buy much more until the price reaches the level that we are happy with," he said, but declined to elaborate on prices or amounts the government would buy.
The official said the rubber would be kept in warehouses while the government secured more deals with foreign buyers.
"The global demand is still strong. A lot of people expressed interest to buy from Thailand and we hope to score more deals soon, both from the EU and China," he told Reuters.
China may enter into an agreement to buy more rubber from Thailand when Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh visited the country early next month, the official told Reuters.
